_about: The formats a project can be and the steps each goes through. A format is a template: its blocks (the row on the section band, kept in work/blocks.json), its steps, its frame shape and, for Shorts, its styles. App steps (kind app) open a part of Video Octopus instead of asking Claude: import, open-cut, open-scenes, open-packaging. The app lights the first step that isn't done. A step is done when one of its files exists in the project, its worklog line is in WORKLOG.md, (json) a key is set in a JSON file, or (kept) a zooms or shots file has an item that isn't a proposal. Claude steps send the skill's slash command plus `ask` into the project's chat (`motion`: "plan" or "build" adds a line on the studio's motion-graphics skills, or what to do without any: server/skills-gh.mjs motionNote); `brief` steps get their text from Video Octopus (server/blocks.mjs). {source} is replaced by the project's source files, {style} by the Short's style. `more` lists single steps that stay reachable from the rail's ⋯ menu. Old format ids stay readable through `aliases` (project.json files are never rewritten). A studio adds its own formats and Short styles in <studio>/.studio/formats.json, merged over these (server/studio.mjs mergeFormats): keep creator-specific styles and skills there, not here. What a creator reads about a step comes from the step itself, one source for the stage chips, the Next and Done cards, the empty states and the first-time help: `stage` (one of the six in `stages`, which never change: Package, Record, Cut, Plan, Build, Polish; Package is optional and never blocks), `name` (the plain name the creator sees; `label` stays for the chat, old logs and the prompts), `what` (one sentence: what it does and who does it; {blocks} becomes the format's own block names), `where` (where its result shows) and `show` {tab: packaging|canvas|scenes|cut|renders|post, target} (what Show me points at). The line a finished step shows is worked out from its files on the server (server/studio.mjs doneLine). A studio's own step without these fields shows its label and a plain line.

prepare.label: Prepare
prepare.name: Clean up
prepare.what: Claude writes the transcript, cuts the ums, long pauses and retakes, then listens to every cut.
prepare.where: a first cut, in the Cut tab
prepare.ask:
Prepare this recording ({source}) in one go: transcribe, rough cut and join check, using the transcribe, rough-cut and join-check skills in that order, without stopping between them.
1. Transcribe the camera file (it carries the mic): the plain pass into work/tr/ (words.json + SRT) and the filler pass the rough-cut skill asks for into work/tr_fill/. {transcribe}
2. Rough cut: find the cuts (work/cuts.json) and apply the default decisions: "cut" items on, "ask" items off, the last take of every retake kept. That writes work/rough.mp4, work/rough_map.json and work/rough_words.json. Don't open a review page and don't wait for me: I veto or restore cuts in Video Octopus's Cut tab.
3. Join check on the rough cut (--map work/rough_map.json --words work/tr/words.json) into work/joins.json and work/edl_fixed.json. From then on work/edl_fixed.json is the cut Video Octopus uses: the Cut tab opens it and the export plays it, so the fixes join-check made there are already applied (say so; don't call them pending).
Then write work/prepare.json: {"cuts": number of cuts made, "saved_s": seconds removed, "ask": [{"t": source seconds where it starts, "end": source seconds where it ends (for anything longer than a word: false starts, a retake, an unfinished ending; Keep and Cut in the Cut tab act on t–end), "what": "…"}] (every cut the rough cut marked "ask", retakes too, whatever you did with it, and anything else that needs my call: the Cut tab lists these under To check), "retakes": number, "joins": number, "clipped": likely clipped joins the fix did not resolve (a join whose fix is in work/edl_fixed.json is fixed, not one for me), "needs_you": asks + clipped, "summary": "Rough cut: 14 cuts, 2 need you"}, add one line to WORKLOG.md, and tell me in three short lines: how much shorter, what needs me (with times), and that the Cut tab shows them. Only stop early if a step fails or needs a decision only I can make.

transcribe.label: Transcribe
transcribe.name: Transcribe
transcribe.what: Claude writes down every word you say, with its time.
transcribe.where: your words, in the Cut tab
transcribe.ask: Transcribe this project's recording ({source}). Put the word times in work/tr/words.json and the SRT next to it. {transcribe}

rough-cut.label: Rough cut
rough-cut.name: Rough cut
rough-cut.what: Claude cuts the ums, long pauses and retakes.
rough-cut.where: a first cut, in the Cut tab
rough-cut.ask: Rough-cut this project's recording ({source}) from work/tr/words.json. Keep the outputs in work/ (rough.mp4, rough_map.json, rough_words.json).

join-check.label: Join check
join-check.name: Join check
join-check.what: Claude listens to every cut and flags the ones that clip a word.
join-check.where: flags on the cuts, in the Cut tab
join-check.ask: Check every join of the rough cut (work/rough_map.json) and write work/joins.json and work/edl_fixed.json.

sections.label: Mark sections
sections.name: Split into sections
sections.what: Claude finds where {blocks} start and end.
sections.where: coloured sections on the band above the timeline

cut-editor.label: Fix in Cut Editor
cut-editor.name: Fix the cut
cut-editor.what: Delete words or drag cut edges yourself, in the Cut tab.
cut-editor.where: your changes, in the Cut tab

lock.label: Lock the cut
lock.name: Lock the cut
lock.what: Claude checks every join one last time and freezes the cut, so scenes can be timed to it.
lock.where: a lock on the Cut tab
lock.ask: Lock the cut. If I saved in the Cut Editor (work/edl_manual.json), render that cut and run join-check on it. When nothing is likely clipped, write "Cut locked (join-check: N joins, 0 clipped)" in WORKLOG.md. If a join still sounds clipped, tell me which ones so I can fix them in the Cut tab.

review.label: Review scenes

steps.label: Plan scenes
steps.name: Plan the scenes
steps.what: Claude writes the scene plan: for each line, what is on screen.
steps.ask:
Write the production sheet for this video from the locked cut, in this studio's own style (BRAND.md, STYLE.md when there is one, memory/style.md). Give every scene the id of the block it belongs to ("block", from work/blocks.json).
This step plans the scenes only, also after I answer your questions or say go ahead: write the sheet, tell me about it and stop. Don't build or render scenes, place sound cues, cut B-roll or place zooms here: Build the intro and Add zooms do those later. If you see where the look should change (the camera off during a demo, boxed for a list) or where a zoom would help, you may offer them as proposals in work/shots.json and work/zooms.json ("by": "claude", "status": "proposed"): they wait for my Keep it / No thanks and don't count as Add zooms.

steps.label: Edit intro
steps.name: Build the intro
steps.what: Claude builds each scene and renders the intro.
steps.where: the video in Renders, each scene in Scenes
steps.ask: Build the intro (the intro block in work/blocks.json) from the production sheet, scene by scene, in this studio's own style: BRAND.md (colours, fonts, the brand files in the library), STYLE.md when there is one, memory/style.md and memory/preferences.md. Build the graphics with the studio's motion-graphics skills where one fits (an explainer or motion-broll skill, if the studio has one). Render short snippets for me to check first, then the intro into renders/ as <project>_intro_v1.mp4 on the production sheet's timeline, so Video Octopus's Scenes tab can show it scene by scene.

steps.label: Zooms
steps.name: Add zooms
steps.what: Claude punches in on your face at the right words.
steps.where: the Zooms lane on the timeline
steps.ask: Place the talking-head zooms (punch-ins on my face) for this project on the locked cut, in work/zooms.json v2 ({"v": 2, "items": […]}, take seconds; each one "target": "camera", "by": "claude", "status": "proposed"). Redo only your own camera punch-ins (target camera, by claude) and keep every other zoom in the file exactly as it is: the plan's screen zooms and mine stay. If there is nothing to zoom on my face (I'm never full frame on camera, say), add "reason": "<why, in a few words to me, e.g. you're never full frame>" to work/zooms.json (still keeping the other zooms). Either way add a WORKLOG.md line that starts with "Add zooms:", so the step counts as done.

This step plans the scenes only, also after I answer your questions or say go ahead: write the sheet, tell me about it and stop. steps.label: Build visuals
steps.name: Build the visuals
steps.what: Claude builds what's on screen for the whole video, over your voice: the screen recording where it shows the thing, real B-roll of what you mention, and graphics. Then it renders it.
steps.where: the video in Renders, each scene in Scenes
steps.ask: Build the visuals for this faceless video from the production sheet, section by section, in this studio's own style: BRAND.md (colours, fonts, the logos and images in the library), STYLE.md when there is one, memory/style.md and memory/preferences.md. There's no face on camera, so every stretch needs something to look at: the screen recording where it shows the thing being talked about (cropped and zoomed so it's readable), real B-roll of what's mentioned (the page, the post, the product), and motion graphics from the studio's motion-graphics skills where one fits. The voice is the spine: don't cut or move it. Render short snippets for me to check first, then the video into renders/ as <project>_faceless_v1.mp4 on the production sheet's timeline, so Video Octopus's Scenes tab can show it scene by scene.
